meta.label: Mobile carriers
meta.attribution: Compiled from public privacy notices, CPNI pages, plan disclosures, terms, coverage pages, regulator actions (FCC enforcement orders), and company annual reports (SEC 10-K filings). Coverage is local, plans change often, and this is not telecom advice. Check your address and bill terms before switching. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Tello Mobile
products.description: A highly configurable prepaid carrier for people who want a small bill and can live with MVNO tradeoffs.

privacy.note: Tello publishes privacy rights and opt-out choices, but still collects carrier account, device, usage, and advertising-related data.

fees.note: Tello's custom-plan page shows low-cost build-your-own plans, including very small talk/data plans and low advertised unlimited pricing.

transparency.note: Tello's terms and help pages emphasize no contract, plan changes, and plan limits in plain public pages.

accessibility.note: Tello is online-first and prepaid; that keeps costs low but offers less retail support than national postpaid carriers.

ethics.note: No-contract, change-anytime prepaid service is consumer-friendly, though Tello is not structured around public-interest giving.

products.name: US Mobile
products.description: A flexible MVNO that lets customers choose among multiple network backbones, with many plans showing taxes and fees included.

privacy.note: US Mobile publishes a privacy policy covering account, device, payment, web, and service-use data plus consumer privacy choices.

fees.note: US Mobile's plans page advertises several plans with taxes and fees included, reducing bill-surprise risk.

transparency.note: US Mobile publicly posts terms and plan details, including billing, taxes, and surcharge language.

accessibility.note: US Mobile offers multiple network options, which can help coverage fit, but it remains a mostly online MVNO.

ethics.note: Clear prepaid-style pricing and network choice are consumer-friendly, though the carrier is not a mission-giving provider.

products.name: Visible
products.description: A simple Verizon-owned prepaid option with taxes and fees included, strongest for people who want a low one-line bill on Verizon coverage.

privacy.note: Visible points customers to a privacy policy and choices, but it is Verizon-owned and collects service, web/app, and usage data.

fees.note: Visible's plan pages advertise unlimited service starting at $25 per month with taxes and fees included.

transparency.note: Visible's homepage and plan pages foreground all-in pricing and plan facts, which helps compare the actual monthly bill.

accessibility.note: Visible runs on Verizon's 5G and 4G LTE networks, with broad network access but online-first support.

ethics.note: All-in prepaid pricing is a positive, but Verizon's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the parent company's accountability record.

products.name: Consumer Cellular
products.description: A simple-plan carrier with AARP benefits and phone support, useful for people who value service help over the absolute lowest bill.

privacy.note: Consumer Cellular publishes a privacy and security policy covering personal, device, service, tax, and account data uses.

fees.note: Consumer Cellular advertises no long-term contract and AARP member discounts, but taxes and fees apply to advertised plans.

transparency.note: Consumer Cellular publishes plans and legal/privacy pages, though some bill totals depend on taxes and fees.

accessibility.note: Consumer Cellular's AARP partnership, no long-term contract, and service positioning make it accessible for older adults and support-sensitive users.

ethics.note: The AARP member benefit and senior-friendly service model are public consumer-access positives, with no major 2024 location-data fine found for this MVNO.

products.name: Google Fi Wireless
products.description: A Google-run carrier with strong account integration and travel features, but also a big-platform privacy tradeoff.

privacy.note: Google Fi publishes a Fi-specific privacy page, CPNI explanation, and privacy choices, but it is tied to the wider Google account ecosystem.

fees.note: Google Fi announced a lower-cost Unlimited Essentials plan, but taxes, fees, financing, and add-ons can still affect the bill.

transparency.note: Google Fi provides support pages explaining Fi privacy, CPNI, and account-data controls in one official place.

accessibility.note: Fi is easy for Google-account users and travelers, but local coverage and device compatibility still need address/device checks.

ethics.note: Fi offers useful privacy documentation and some network protections, but dependence on a major ad-tech platform limits public-interest confidence.

products.name: Mint Mobile
products.description: A recognizable prepaid carrier with low promotional prices and bulk-payment savings, now within the T-Mobile orbit.

privacy.note: Mint's privacy policy describes personal, device, account, marketing, and sharing practices rather than a minimal-data carrier model.

fees.note: Mint advertises low monthly prices, but many offers depend on introductory or multi-month prepaid terms and taxes/fees can be extra.

transparency.note: Mint posts plan terms publicly, including limitations, renewal terms, and reduced speeds after high-speed data allotments.

accessibility.note: Mint's online-first prepaid model is easy to buy, but bulk prepayment and coverage fit make it less accessible for some users.

ethics.note: Low prepaid pricing is useful, but T-Mobile's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the ownership family's accountability record.

products.name: Cricket Wireless
products.description: A major prepaid brand with retail presence and taxes-included monthly plan pricing, owned by AT&T.

privacy.note: Cricket's privacy policy says it shares information with AT&T companies and covers advertising, analytics, and account/service data uses.

fees.note: Cricket says monthly plan charges include state and local taxes, which makes many prepaid comparisons easier.

transparency.note: Cricket publicly posts taxes/fees explanations and terms, making the bill structure more inspectable than many postpaid plans.

accessibility.note: Cricket has broad AT&T-network access and retail/prepaid availability, which helps users who want in-person support.

ethics.note: Taxes-included prepaid pricing helps consumers, but AT&T's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the parent company's accountability record.

products.name: Metro by T-Mobile
products.description: A mainstream prepaid brand with taxes and regulatory fees included on many plans, backed by T-Mobile's network.

privacy.note: Metro uses T-Mobile privacy notices and choices, which cover service, device, account, advertising, and CPNI data practices.

fees.note: Metro says applicable taxes and regulatory fees are included in the advertised plan price for its prepaid plans.

transparency.note: Metro publicly explains its taxes-and-fees inclusion and no-contract prepaid positioning.

accessibility.note: Metro combines T-Mobile network access with prepaid retail availability, making it more accessible than online-only MVNOs.

ethics.note: No-contract and taxes-included pricing help, but T-Mobile's 2024 FCC location-data fine weighs against the parent company's accountability record.

products.name: CREDO Mobile
products.description: A mission-oriented mobile provider that turns bills into donations for progressive nonprofits, with a higher-cost tradeoff.

privacy.note: CREDO publishes a privacy policy covering account communications, service data, activism communications, and customer privacy choices.

fees.note: CREDO's mission model is not mainly a low-cost offering; its value claim centers on donations rather than cheapest monthly service.

transparency.note: CREDO publishes donation history and mission pages that make the social-impact claim inspectable.

accessibility.note: CREDO is US-focused and mission-led, but its niche positioning and likely higher bill make it less broadly accessible than budget MVNOs.

ethics.note: CREDO reports more than $95 million donated to progressive nonprofits and lets members vote on monthly donation recipients.

products.name: T-Mobile
products.description: A national carrier with broad access and strong network convenience, but high data exposure and accountability concerns.

privacy.note: T-Mobile's privacy notice covers extensive personal, account, device, location, CPNI, advertising, and sharing practices.

fees.note: T-Mobile's current plan pages state that displayed plan prices can exclude taxes, surcharges, and fees that vary by location.

transparency.note: T-Mobile posts current privacy and plan disclosures, but plan-generation changes and fee exclusions make comparison harder.

accessibility.note: T-Mobile is a national carrier with broad network reach, retail support, and mainstream device/service availability.

ethics.note: The FCC fined T-Mobile more than $80 million in 2024 over illegally sharing access to customer location data.

products.name: Verizon
products.description: A national carrier with broad coverage and retail access, but usually a weaker fit for privacy, fees, and accountability values.

privacy.note: Verizon's privacy policy covers broad collection and use of customer, device, service, advertising, and account data, with privacy choices.

fees.note: Verizon's unlimited-plan pages and surcharge support pages state that taxes, government fees, and Verizon surcharges may be added.

transparency.note: Verizon posts detailed privacy, CPNI, and surcharge pages, but the number of fees and add-ons makes total-price comparison complex.

accessibility.note: Verizon is a national carrier with broad network access, retail support, and mainstream device/service availability.

ethics.note: The FCC fined Verizon almost $47 million in 2024 over illegally sharing access to customer location data.

products.name: AT&T
products.description: A national carrier with broad access and device support, but a weak fit for people optimizing around privacy, fees, and accountability.

privacy.note: AT&T's privacy notice covers wireless, internet, voice, apps, data use, advertising choices, and CPNI-related uses.

fees.note: AT&T's unlimited-plan disclosures say monthly AT&T fees and government taxes are extra, including cost-recovery and other fees.

transparency.note: AT&T publishes privacy and fee schedules, but separate AT&T fees, government taxes, add-ons, and plan changes make bill comparison harder.

accessibility.note: AT&T is a national carrier with broad network access, retail support, and mainstream device/service availability.

ethics.note: The FCC fined AT&T more than $57 million in 2024 over illegally sharing access to customer location data.

products.name: Straight Talk Wireless
products.description: A Walmart-partnered prepaid brand run by Verizon's TracFone unit, easy to find but with a recent FCC data-breach settlement behind it.

privacy.note: Straight Talk's privacy link redirects to Verizon, whose full privacy policy covers the 'Verizon Value' brands including Straight Talk and says 'Certain Verizon Value brands share information that identifies you with our partner, Prove' for identity and credit checks (opt-out available).

fees.note: Straight Talk's all-plans page has tiered Silver, Gold and Platinum Unlimited plans and a Lifeline discount for eligible customers, but states 'Taxes and fees apply' and that discounts, taxes and fees appear only at checkout.

transparency.note: Plan features differ by network ('Some plan features are only available to customers on the Verizon network'), surcharges vary by state, and taxes appear at checkout, so the true monthly total takes some digging; FCC broadband labels are offered by ZIP code.

accessibility.note: Straight Talk bundles Walmart+ perks on higher plans, offers a Lifeline discount on plans with at least 4.5 GB, and notes that some plan features are only available on the Verizon network, so coverage and features depend on which network a line uses.

ethics.note: In July 2024 the FCC settled with TracFone, which runs Straight Talk, for a $16,000,000 civil penalty over three 2021-2023 data breaches via customer-facing APIs that exposed customer data and led to unauthorized port-outs; the order names Straight Talk as a TracFone brand.

products.name: Total Wireless
products.description: A Verizon-owned prepaid brand with taxes and fees included and a five-year price guarantee, carrying the same TracFone data-breach history as its sister brands.

privacy.note: Total Wireless's privacy link redirects to Verizon; the full Verizon privacy policy lists Total Wireless among the Verizon Value brands and describes sharing identifying data with the identity-verification partner Prove unless the customer opts out.

fees.note: Total's plans page lists one line at $25/mo (MAX 5G BYO) to $60/mo (ALL ACCESS) with Auto Pay, and the price-guarantee footnote says 'Taxes and fees included.'

transparency.note: The plans page shows per-line prices for 1-5 lines in one table and spells out the 5-year price guarantee's limits (it excludes one-time charges and can be lost if service lapses or the plan changes).

accessibility.note: Total lists 'Verizon 5G network' among standard benefits and offers free-phone and bring-your-own-phone paths with no contracts.

ethics.note: The all-in price guarantee is consumer-friendly, but the FCC's July 2024 TracFone consent decree ($16,000,000 penalty over three data breaches) lists Total Wireless among the TracFone brands.

products.name: Tracfone
products.description: The long-running basic prepaid brand, useful for small and occasional-use plans, and the company at the centre of the FCC's 2024 data-breach settlement.

privacy.note: Tracfone is one of the Verizon Value brands covered by Verizon's full privacy policy, which describes sharing identifying data with the partner Prove for identity and credit decisions and offers a Tracfone 'Your Privacy Choices' opt-out page.

fees.note: Tracfone sells basic plans alongside an unlimited plan at '$45/mo with Auto-Refill', a 6-month bring-your-own-phone plan for $135, and Lifeline and military discounts; taxes and fees are added at checkout.

transparency.note: Plan pages carry FCC broadband labels, but prices are spread across promotions, auto-refill discounts and add-on cards, and taxes are only shown at checkout.

accessibility.note: Tracfone keeps basic low-usage plans, a Lifeline discount on plans with at least 4.5 GB, and a 10% military discount; its unlimited plan is 'only available on the Verizon network'.

ethics.note: TracFone Wireless agreed to a $16,000,000 civil penalty and a mandated information-security compliance plan to settle FCC investigations into three 2021-2023 breaches that exposed customer PI and CPNI and enabled unauthorized port-outs.

products.name: Boost Mobile
products.description: A low-price prepaid carrier owned by EchoStar, now running largely on AT&T's radio network, with a privacy notice that discloses selling data to brokers.

privacy.note: Boost's privacy notice says 'We sell or share these categories of personal information to data analytics providers, advertising partners and/or networks, social networks, and data brokers', with an opt-out portal.

fees.note: Boost's plans page advertises Unlimited at $25/mo 'forever' including a $5 AutoPay discount ($30 without), with higher tiers up to $60/mo; it notes 'Taxes and fees apply.'

transparency.note: Boost states the AutoPay and non-AutoPay price for each plan, the 30 GB premium-data threshold before speeds may drop, and a 30-day money-back guarantee on the plans page.

accessibility.note: EchoStar's 2025 annual report says Boost now operates as a 'Hybrid MNO' that runs its own 5G core but uses AT&T's network services, sold online and through third-party and big-box retail; it reported 7.511 million wireless subscribers at end-2025.

ethics.note: Boost's plans page offers a 30-day money-back guarantee and no contracts unless financing a device; no FCC privacy enforcement against Boost under EchoStar was found in this check, but the privacy notice's data-broker sales weigh against it.

products.name: Spectrum Mobile
products.description: Charter's mobile service on Verizon's network, priced with no added taxes but sold only to Spectrum Internet customers, under a data-hungry privacy policy.

privacy.note: Spectrum's privacy policy says 'information about your general or precise location and Internet Usage Information may be used to provide you with marketing and advertising from Spectrum and its business partners', and that mobile data includes non-Spectrum WiFi networks a device connects to.

fees.note: Spectrum lists Unlimited lines at $30/mo, Unlimited Plus at $40 and Plus Premium at $50 with 'no contracts, added taxes or hidden fees', but the service requires Spectrum Internet, which the page prices from $30/mo.

transparency.note: The mobile page states per-line prices and the no-added-taxes promise plainly, but much of the offer is first-year and bundle pricing that depends on the internet plan chosen.

accessibility.note: Charter's 2025 annual report says Spectrum Mobile is an MVNO 'using Verizon’s network' plus Spectrum WiFi and CBRS; the Spectrum page says it is available only to Spectrum Internet customers, which limits who can switch.

ethics.note: Charter admitted in a July 2024 FCC consent decree that it failed to notify more than 1,000 911 call centres of a February 2023 outage and missed outage-reporting deadlines, and paid a $15,000,000 civil penalty.

products.name: Xfinity Mobile
products.description: Comcast's mobile service on Verizon's network, cheap for existing Xfinity Internet households but locked to the bundle and to Comcast's ad-supported data practices.

privacy.note: The Xfinity privacy policy (effective April 23, 2026) lists 'Geolocation information that indicates where your device is at a specific point in time when you use Xfinity Mobile' and DNS and traffic activity among collected data, used for marketing and advertising with preference controls.

fees.note: Xfinity advertises Mobile Select at $0/mo for the first year, then $30/mo with Xfinity Internet, and Mobile Plus at $15 then $45/mo; 'taxes and fees, and other applicable charges extra' after year one, and Xfinity Internet is required.

transparency.note: Pricing leans on first-year promotions, an internet-customer discount, and device-payment conditions spelled out in fine print, which makes the long-run bill harder to read.

accessibility.note: Comcast's 2025 annual report says its wireless service runs over 'Verizon’s wireless network' plus WiFi hotspots and is offered only as part of bundles for qualifying broadband customers; Xfinity says the service is exclusive to Xfinity Internet members.

ethics.note: In November 2025 Comcast agreed with the FCC to a $1,500,000 voluntary contribution and a vendor-oversight compliance plan after a former vendor's breach exposed Comcast cable subscribers' personal information.

products.name: Ting Mobile
products.description: A small, plain-spoken MVNO with pay-as-you-go and low unlimited plans, now part of the DISH/EchoStar family and sharing its data practices.

privacy.note: Ting's privacy notice says 'We disclose your personal information to DISH affiliates' such as Boost Mobile and Sling TV, and that it sells or shares identifiers and activity data with analytics, advertising and data-broker parties.

fees.note: Ting lists Flex pay-as-you-go at $10/mo per line plus $5/GB, and Unlimited at $25/mo per line, with no data overage charges; taxes are added on top.

transparency.note: Ting's terms say plainly 'We don’t charge tax, we collect it. Taxes, regulatory fees, E911 fees and so on are not included in Ting rates.', and plan pages carry FCC broadband labels.

accessibility.note: Ting is online-only, needs an unlocked phone, and advertises nationwide LTE and 5G coverage with SIM or eSIM.

ethics.note: No contracts, no prepayment and no data overage charges are consumer-friendly; Ting is not a mission or giving carrier.

products.name: Cape
products.description: A privacy-first carrier that collects minimal data, deletes call logs after a day and rotates network identifiers, at a premium price.

privacy.note: Cape's privacy principles say 'We will never sell your data. Period.' and that it collects the minimum needed; its site says call and text logs are deleted after 1 day and it offers IMSI identifier rotation.

fees.note: Cape's single Privacy Unlimited plan is listed at $99/mo, with $70/mo locked in for early adopters, well above budget MVNOs.

transparency.note: Cape publishes a plain-language privacy summary (updated August 18, 2026), says it will notify subscribers of legal process when permitted, and its terms promise to 'only charge what you see on your bill – no hidden fees'.

accessibility.note: Cape claims nationwide 5G/4G coverage but is online-only, requires a compatible recent phone (Android 13+ or iPhone XR/11 and newer) and users aged 18 or over, and may slow data after 50 GB.

ethics.note: TechCrunch reported Cape's $99/month open beta in March 2025 and its commitment not to track or sell data; Cape says it partners with the EFF to offer free and discounted service to journalists and activists and is donating over $100,000 to GrapheneOS.

products.name: Assurance Wireless
products.description: A T-Mobile-owned Lifeline provider offering free monthly service to eligible low-income households, with T-Mobile's privacy terms and record.

privacy.note: Assurance Wireless links its privacy policy to T-Mobile's privacy notice, which lists Assurance Wireless among T-Mobile's companies and covers broad account, device, usage, advertising and CPNI data practices.

fees.note: Assurance advertises free monthly Lifeline service with 10 GB high-speed data and unlimited talk and text for eligible customers, with 'No activation fees'.

transparency.note: The page discloses that Lifeline customers may see lower speeds than others during congestion, that offers vary by state, and links to its annual certification requirement.

accessibility.note: Lifeline is open only to households at or below 135% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Guidelines or in programs such as SNAP or Medicaid, with one discount per household; Assurance runs on T-Mobile's network.

ethics.note: Free Lifeline service is a real access benefit, but parent T-Mobile was fined more than $80 million by the FCC in April 2024 for sharing customers' location data without consent.

products.name: Ultra Mobile
products.description: A T-Mobile-owned prepaid brand built around free international calling and multilingual support, with prepaid bulk-buy pricing like sister brand Mint.

privacy.note: Ultra's privacy notice (archived July 2026) says it may sell aggregate or non-personal data 'to any third party for any purpose', but extends the California do-not-sell-or-share choice 'to all our customers regardless of their state of residence.'

fees.note: Ultra's homepage (archived August 2026) listed a 4GB plan at $19/mo and Unlimited at $49/mo, plus annual plans from $10/mo; 'Upfront payment req’d; taxes & fees extra.'

transparency.note: Ultra posts FCC broadband labels and plan terms, but promotional renewal credits, upfront multi-month payments and extra taxes make the monthly figure less direct.

accessibility.note: Ultra sells online and in stores, runs on the T-Mobile 5G network, includes unlimited talk to 90+ international destinations and has a care team that 'supports English, Spanish and Mandarin'.

ethics.note: Ultra is one of T-Mobile's prepaid brands (per T-Mobile's 2025 10-K); the FCC fined T-Mobile more than $80 million in April 2024 for sharing access to customers' location data without consent.
